sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily GitHub Trending snapshot at 2026-11-18 17:39 UTC; date range 2026-11-18 through 2026-11-18 UTC (in progress). Ranking is descending by daily Trending stars gained.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: AI-agent software is the clearest signal today: security and development skill bundles, research automation, and agent-facing software interfaces occupy most of the highest-gain spots. Claude-BugHunter leads at +2,322 stars, followed by PaperOrchestra at +1,529.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and authorized external red-team work, spanning vulnerability classes and enterprise attack surfaces.
sections.why_notable: The largest daily star gain in this snapshot; its README describes a large, structured security-testing skill collection.

sections.title: google-research/paper-orchestra
sections.description: A multi-agent pipeline that turns research ideas and experiment logs into submission-ready LaTeX papers.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain; its specialized agents cover outlining, literature synthesis, writing, refinement, and plotting.

sections.title: affaan-m/ECC
sections.description: An agent-harness toolkit combining skills, memory, security, and research-first development across coding agents.
sections.why_notable: One of the day's largest gains and a prominent example of packaging reusable agent workflow and performance practices.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An agent skill that researches recent discussion across social, video, news, prediction-market, and web sources.
sections.why_notable: Strong daily momentum for a cross-source research workflow that emphasizes grounded synthesis.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: A coding-agent development methodology built from composable skills and workflow instructions.
sections.why_notable: A high-gain, established skills framework, reinforcing demand for structured agent-assisted development rather than prompt-only usage.

sections.title: sveltejs/svelte
sections.description: A JavaScript framework for building web applications.
sections.why_notable: The strongest traditional frontend-framework signal among the selected entries, a useful counterpoint to the agent-heavy list.

sections.title: getarcaneapp/arcane
sections.description: A modern interface for managing Docker environments.
sections.why_notable: A clear self-hosting and container-operations project with more than five hundred stars gained today.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: A toolkit for giving software agent-friendly command-line interfaces to existing applications.
sections.why_notable: Its README centers on generated CLI harnesses and demos of agents creating real artifacts, representing the agent-native interface theme.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: Design and build skills for Google Stitch, following the Agent Skills open standard.
sections.why_notable: Shows design-tool workflows joining the cross-agent skills ecosystem, with documented compatibility across several coding agents.

sections.title: NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator
sections.description: A framework for testing agent skills and plugins for quality, overlap, compatibility, security, and task impact.
sections.why_notable: Adds an evaluation and CI angle to the agent-skill trend; its README describes quality checks and with/without-skill task comparisons.

sections.title: cursor/plugins
sections.description: Cursor's plugin specification and collection of official plugins.
sections.why_notable: A platform-level signal that coding-agent extensibility is being formalized through plugins.

sections.title: n8n-io/n8n
sections.description: A workflow automation platform combining visual building, custom code, integrations, and AI capabilities.
sections.why_notable: Ties for the final selected gain; it represents the established automation platform side of agent-enabled workflows.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent skills and harnesses: Claude-BugHunter, ECC, Superpowers, Stitch Skills, NVIDIA SkillEvaluator, and Cursor plugins point to reusable skills, plugin ecosystems, and evaluation. Agent-facing interfaces and automation: CLI-Anything, Arcane, and n8n reflect machine-usable software and workflow automation. Research and synthesis: PaperOrchestra and last30days-skill automate specialized research pipelines. Languages among the 12 selected repos: Python 5, TypeScript 3, JavaScript 2, Go 1, Shell 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's list suggests agent tooling is broadening from model interaction into reusable skills, quality measurement, research workflows, and software interfaces. The large daily gains are concentrated in agent-related repositories, but Svelte and Arcane show that conventional frontend and self-hosted infrastructure projects remain part of the day's momentum too.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, captured 2026-11-18 17:39 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository metadata and default-branch refs for all entries; GitHub Search API queries Claude-BugHunter and pushed:>=2026-11-17 stars:>100. Daily gains are the matching Trending-page stars-today values; the UTC window was still in progress.
